newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May housing completions fell 6.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May housing completions fell 6.5 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:

Commerce said May completions of single-family homes fell 6.8 percent after a revised 0.5 percent rise in April and a revised 8.8 percent decrease in March. Previously, the department said single-family completions rose 0.1 percent in April and decreased 9.1 percent in March.

May multi-family unit completions fell 5.2 percent after a revised 3.2 percent decline in April and a 3.2 percent increase in March. The department revised April multi-family unit completions from a 1.0 percent drop and March from a 2.0 decline.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis rose in May to 111,100 units from a revised 110,400 units in April and from a revised 109,600 units in March. In May 1996, actual completions were reported at 114,600 units. The department previously reported April completions at 108,200 and 108,000 in March.

Privately-owned housing units under construction rose in May to aly adjusted 816,000 units from a revised 815,000 in April and from a revised 814,000 units in March. They compare with 826,000 units under construction in May 1996. The department revised both April and March housing under construction from 817,000.
